rhetorical_functions.label: Position a claim
rhetorical_functions.definition: State or locate the paper's own defensible position.

rhetorical_functions.label: Qualify a claim
rhetorical_functions.definition: Set confidence, scope, or conditions on an assertion.

rhetorical_functions.label: Introduce evidence
rhetorical_functions.definition: Present a source, observation, result, or estimate.

rhetorical_functions.label: Interpret evidence
rhetorical_functions.definition: Explain what evidence supports without exceeding it.

rhetorical_functions.label: Compare findings
rhetorical_functions.definition: Make a relevant similarity between results or sources explicit.

rhetorical_functions.label: Contrast findings
rhetorical_functions.definition: Make a relevant difference between results or sources explicit.

rhetorical_functions.label: Synthesize sources
rhetorical_functions.definition: Integrate multiple sources into a higher-level account.

rhetorical_functions.label: Identify a gap
rhetorical_functions.definition: Specify an unresolved question or bounded absence.

rhetorical_functions.label: State a limitation
rhetorical_functions.definition: Describe a constraint and its consequence for inference.

rhetorical_functions.label: Recommend action
rhetorical_functions.definition: Propose research or practice proportionate to evidence.

rhetorical_functions.label: Make a causal claim
rhetorical_functions.definition: Attribute an outcome to a cause under a credible design.

rhetorical_functions.label: Define scope
rhetorical_functions.definition: Set population, context, time, concept, or analytic boundary.

rhetorical_functions.label: Establish context
rhetorical_functions.definition: Frame the problem, debate, or practical setting that motivates the work.

rhetorical_functions.label: Describe a method
rhetorical_functions.definition: Report sampling, material, procedure, model, or evaluation design.

rhetorical_functions.label: Justify a method
rhetorical_functions.definition: Explain why a method fits the question, unit, or uncertainty.

rhetorical_functions.label: Report a null or inconclusive result
rhetorical_functions.definition: Report non-significance, equivalence, absence, or imprecision without overclaiming.

rhetorical_functions.label: Describe an association
rhetorical_functions.definition: Report covariation or prediction without assigning cause.

rhetorical_functions.label: Distinguish association from causation
rhetorical_functions.definition: Make explicit why evidence does or does not identify a causal effect.

rhetorical_functions.label: Attribute a source
rhetorical_functions.definition: Keep a claim, interpretation, or definition attached to its source.

rhetorical_functions.label: Paraphrase with attribution
rhetorical_functions.definition: Restate a source-dependent proposition independently while preserving citation duty.

rhetorical_functions.label: Report uncertainty
rhetorical_functions.definition: Report intervals, sensitivity, heterogeneity, or measurement boundaries.

rhetorical_functions.label: Interpret qualitative evidence
rhetorical_functions.definition: Connect qualitative material to a bounded pattern or interpretation.

rhetorical_functions.label: Respond to a reviewer
rhetorical_functions.definition: Address review comments through revisions, evidence, or reasoned explanation.

rhetorical_functions.label: State a contribution
rhetorical_functions.definition: Describe empirical, conceptual, or methodological value without unsupported priority claims.

claim_strengths.definition: Supported assertion explicitly limited by scope or conditions.
Direct assertion supported by relevant empirical evidence.
Cause-effect assertion requiring a credible causal design.

evidence_requirements.definition: Organizational or definitional wording; no empirical support is implied.
Background, theory, or a bounded source context.
A reported association, comparison, estimate, or observed pattern.
Evidence directly tests the stated proposition under the study design.
Multiple independent lines of relevant evidence agree.

domains.label: Humanities and interpretive inquiry
domains.definition: Textual, historical, conceptual, and interpretive scholarship.

domains.label: Social and behavioral research
domains.definition: Research on people, institutions, societies, and behavior.

domains.label: Quantitative empirical research
domains.definition: Statistical estimation, comparison, prediction, and uncertainty.

domains.label: Qualitative inquiry
domains.definition: Interpretive analysis of interviews, observations, texts, and cases.

domains.label: Experimental and natural science
domains.definition: Experimental, observational, and measurement-centered scientific work.

domains.label: Engineering and computing
domains.definition: Designed systems, algorithms, benchmarks, and technical evaluation.

domains.label: Legal and policy scholarship
domains.definition: Doctrinal, comparative, regulatory, and policy analysis.

domains.label: Business and management
domains.definition: Organizations, markets, operations, and managerial research.

risk_levels.definition: Wording unlikely to overstate evidence when slots are filled accurately.
Wording requires explicit attention to scope or evidence quality.
Causal, prescriptive, or otherwise consequential wording requiring strong checks.
